mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted effect is not robust during periods of rising commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages, or the effect reverses when unemployment rises above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1% and 5%, respectively, for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls >1% and HOUST falls >5% in the same month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present when monetary policy is easing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for at least six months signals entrenched labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and consumer purchasing power, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate policy easing and eventual recovery.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 6% for at least 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during prolonged high-unemployment regimes, or the effect reverses when inflation spikes above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by the residual of disposable income minus consumption, approximated by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio) above its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio exceeds 12-month average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the savings ratio is elevated for four months, or the effect is absent during periods of fiscal tightening.
